params.body:
`hand.mjs policy sign` signs the next version of the gateway's policy log on the owner's YubiKey, on the laptop, and hands it to Portal. Portal kept it only on `POST /api/ingest/control/policy`, which sits behind the ingest token. The laptop holds no Portal token since 5 October 2026, so the signed version could not be delivered: the same gap the working set had (#360).

**`POST /api/ingest/policy-version` (new, no token, throttled 10 per minute)** goes to the same `PolicyLogController::store`. The token adds nothing:

- `PolicyLog::check` verifies the signature against the owner's or Elixir's key in the DID document.
- `keep` holds the chain to one direction: a version must name the hash before it, and an applied version stays.

A delivery is recorded as via `laptop`, like a read-token delivery was. Elixir keeps using the fabric route.

Tests: `PolicyLogTest` passes 9 of 9. The new case: an owner-signed version is kept without a token, and a version signed by another key is refused.
